items.title: CVE-2026-132224: Optimizely Optimizely Web Experimentation External Control of Critical State Data Vulnerability
items.one_liner: A critical flaw in Optimizely allows attackers to inject malicious JavaScript into customer websites.
items.summary: Optimizely Web Experimentation contains a vulnerability in its account signup flow that allows attackers to impersonate users and modify Project JavaScript. This flaw enables the distribution of malicious, attacker-controlled JavaScript to browsers visiting customer websites. CISA has mandated federal remediation for this issue by November 27, 2026.
items.bottom_line: Organizations using Optimizely must treat this as a high-priority supply-chain risk and apply vendor patches immediately.

items.title: CVE-2026-132165: Drupal Drupal Core Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

items.summary: Drupal Core contains a vulnerability in its installer that allows unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code or take over sites. items.title: OpenAI and Cisco Unveil AI-Assisted Linux Security Tool to Block Exploits Before Patching
items.one_liner: Shirudo provides a way to deploy eBPF-based security mitigations for Linux vulnerabilities without needing to patch or restart services.
items.summary: OpenAI and Cisco have launched Shirudo, an open-source Linux runtime security tool that uses AI agents to deploy eBPF-based shields. The tool allows security teams to block specific exploit paths without requiring system restarts or downtime while patches are being developed. It leverages the Tetragon platform to inject code mitigations that are cryptographically signed and verified before execution. This approach aims to provide temporary protection for vulnerable services against active threats.
items.bottom_line: Security teams can now use AI-generated eBPF shields to neutralize exploits in real-time, significantly reducing the urgency of emergency patching cycles.

items.title: CrowdStrike agrees to buy Zscaler for $43.9 billion in network security expansion
items.one_liner: CrowdStrike is acquiring Zscaler for $43.9 billion to unite endpoint security and zero-trust network access for modern cloud architectures.
items.summary: CrowdStrike has agreed to acquire Zscaler in an all-stock transaction valued at approximately $43.9 billion to merge endpoint protection with cloud network security. The acquisition combines CrowdStrike's device and cloud workload monitoring with Zscaler's zero-trust network access control, addressing security requirements as corporate systems and AI agents connect directly to cloud applications. CrowdStrike plans to integrate device telemetry with network connection logs and cross-sell both platforms to Zscaler's roughly 8,000 customers. Zscaler CEO Jay Chaudhry will continue leading the business and join CrowdStrike's board upon closing, which is expected in the second half of fiscal 2028 pending regulatory and shareholder approvals.

items.title: Huawei found guilty of stealing trade secrets but acquitted of racketeering
items.one_liner: Huawei was convicted in a US court of trade secret theft and bank fraud, but was acquitted of racketeering charges.
items.summary: Huawei has been found guilty in a US court of conspiracy to steal trade secrets and bank fraud, alongside violating US sanctions, following a two-month trial in Brooklyn. However, jurors declined to convict the Chinese technology giant of the more serious overarching racketeering conspiracy charge under RICO. Federal prosecutors argued the firm spent decades utilizing lies and theft to gain a competitive business edge, while Huawei's defense team maintained the company's success stemmed from hard work and innovation and plans to appeal the verdict. Sentencing is scheduled for September 2027.
items.bottom_line: A US jury convicted Huawei of trade secret theft and bank fraud but acquitted the firm of the racketeering charge.

items.title: VirtualBox Process Hardening on Windows 2026 Edition: What’s a Single Bit Between Friends?
items.one_liner: A new VirtualBox vulnerability (CVE-2026-87268) allows arbitrary code execution by abusing .NET memory-based assembly loading to bypass process hardening.
items.summary: Google Project Zero researcher identified new bypasses for Oracle VirtualBox's process hardening on Windows, specifically focusing on CVE-2026-87268. The vulnerability exploits the .NET Framework's ability to load assemblies from memory buffers, which bypasses DLL loader hooks used by VirtualBox to verify loaded modules. By leveraging this behavior, an attacker can load arbitrary code into a protected process. This research highlights the risks of relying on standard runtime features to enforce process security.
items.bottom_line: VirtualBox's process hardening can be bypassed by abusing .NET Framework features to load unsigned code, rendering existing DLL verification checks ineffective.

items.one_liner: A privilege escalation vulnerability in Everest Forms allows low-privileged users to become administrators by activating arbitrary plugins.
items.summary: The Everest Forms plugin for WordPress (versions up to 3.6.4) contains a critical authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated attackers to escalate privileges. By exploiting a missing authorization check, an attacker with 'everest_forms_create_forms' capabilities can trigger the activation of any inactive plugin on the server. If the plugin follows a specific naming convention, this can lead to full administrator-level access. The vulnerability requires a site administrator to have previously delegated specific capabilities to a lower-privileged role.
items.bottom_line: Administrators should immediately update Everest Forms and audit user roles to ensure the 'everest_forms_create_forms' capability is not assigned to untrusted accounts.

items.title: CVE-2026-120539 (CRITICAL 9.8): The Restrictions for BuddyPress plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Remote Code Execution in all versions u…
items.one_liner: A critical RCE vulnerability in the Restrictions for BuddyPress plugin allows unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary PHP code via GET requests.
items.summary: The Restrictions for BuddyPress plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to unauthenticated Remote Code Execution in all versions up to and including 1.5.4, carrying a critical CVSS score of 9.8. The flaw stems from the plugin splicing attacker-controlled request URIs into a double-quoted string and evaluating it via eval(), where PHP interpolation executes payloads in URL paths like {${...}}. Because the vulnerable code evaluates before any authentication checks when BuddyPress and Paid Memberships Pro are active, unauthenticated attackers can execute arbitrary code with a single GET request.
key_facts: Affected versions: Up to and including 1.5.4

items.title: VMware patches critical vCenter authentication bypass and ESX flaws
items.one_liner: Broadcom patched 23 VMware vulnerabilities, including critical authentication bypasses and code execution flaws.
items.summary: Broadcom has released security updates addressing 23 vulnerabilities in VMware products, including a critical authentication bypass in vCenter (CVE-2026-123903, CVSS 9.8) and multiple code execution flaws in ESX hosts. The vCenter vulnerability allows unauthenticated attackers with network access to gain unauthorized access to the VMware Directory Service. Additionally, two critical ESX vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-123910 and CVE-2026-123911) allow code execution via the I/O filter service. items.one_liner: Git 2.56.1 and backports fix six critical security flaws, including code execution during cloning and path traversal.
items.summary: The Git project has released security patches across multiple maintenance series, culminating in Git 2.56.1, to address six vulnerabilities including arbitrary code execution, path traversal, and stack corruption. CVE-2026-111760 involves an integer truncation vulnerability during index handling that permits an attacker-controlled Git server to overwrite repository metadata or execute code during cloning. Other fixed issues include path traversal via protocol v2 HEAD advertisements (CVE-2026-113408), stack corruption from excessive GPG signatures during merges (CVE-2026-114467), and out-of-bounds reads when applying compressed binary patches. Administrators and developers should update Git installations and dependent applications immediately.

items.one_liner: A flawed CSRF protection mechanism in WPIDE allows unauthenticated attackers to achieve RCE by targeting logged-in administrators.
items.summary: WPIDE versions 3.6.0 through 3.6.4 are vulnerable to an unauthenticated Remote Code Execution (RCE) exploit via a CSRF nonce bypass (CVE-2026-124251). The vulnerability stems from a security check that only validates nonces when the URL parameter matches the main 'wpide' slug, allowing attackers to bypass protection by using submenu slugs containing '#/'. An attacker can trick a logged-in administrator into saving and executing malicious PHP snippets, leading to full server-side code execution. The issue was addressed in version 3.6.5.
items.bottom_line: If you manage WordPress sites using WPIDE, ensure you are on version 3.6.5 or higher to prevent unauthenticated RCE via CSRF.

items.summary: The PRC-nexus threat actor ARMORY CASTLE (formerly UNC5221) exploited a zero-day vulnerability, CVE-2026-123890, in VMware vCenter Server deployments. Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant published these findings to assist defenders in detecting multi-zero-day campaigns.

items.title: What Is Preemptive MDR? A Guide For Security Leaders

items.summary: Preemptive Managed Detection and Response (MDR) connects exposure context, threat intelligence, AI-assisted investigation, and human expertise to help security teams prioritize vulnerabilities before exploitation occurs. AI accelerates this process by gathering and correlating logs and user activity across multiple systems.
items.bottom_line: Security leaders can reduce repeat compromises by tying MDR investigations directly to vulnerability prioritization and cross-environment remediation.

items.summary: Overview On October 20, 2026, Python’s security team advised users to update Python packaging tools following the eMudhra / emSign certificate authority incident. Python security announcement Google confirmed that eight intermediate CA certificates had private keys generated with insufficient randomness. Anyone who recovers such a key can create certificates that impersonate websites to a client that still accepts the affected chain. An attacker must also intercept or redirect the victim’s connection to exploit that trust.

Now it all lands in one place, and I can leave notes on it. npx github:krispuckett/rounds --demo The demo is six of my public projects and the real notes I left on them. It runs in its own folder and doesn't touch your setup.
